original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs are bar k-visibility graphs, where vertices are horizontal bars and two bars are adjacent exactly when some vertical segment between them intersects at most k other bars.
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Open Problem 19: "Characterize bar k-visibility graphs." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct target problem and captures the core geometric rule from the paper: vertices are represented by horizontal bars, and adjacency is determined by the existence of a vertical sightline crossing at most k intervening bars. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: To make the question stand-alone, k should be stated as a given/fixed parameter; the surrounding discussion treats ordinary bar visibility graphs as the k = 0 case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
The representation should be specified as a set S of pairwise disjoint horizontal line segments in the plane. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
The paper's formal definition uses a one-to-one association between vertices of G and bars in S; your draft leaves that correspondence implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The relevant notion here is the strong-visibility version: adjacency is witnessed by a vertical segment between the two bars, not by a positive-width visibility rectangle. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The condition is most faithfully stated as: uv is an edge if and only if there exists a vertical segment between the bars for u and v that intersects at most k other bars from the representation. Your draft is essentially correct, but the ambient set of bars is not explicitly named. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The paper poses this specifically as a characterization problem for the graph class, distinct from the nearby forbidden-subgraph, regularity, chromatic-number, thickness, crossing-number, and genus questions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: For a fixed integer k ≥ 0, characterize the graphs G for which there exists a set S of pairwise disjoint horizontal line segments in the plane, in one-to-one correspondence with V(G), such that for distinct vertices u,v ∈ V(G), uv ∈ E(G) if and only if there is a vertical segment with one endpoint on the bar for u and the other on the bar for v that intersects at most k other bars of S. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: The draft clearly targets the bar k-visibility characterization problem in Section 3.3 rather than any neighboring problem. The nearest official formulation is Open Problem 19, and the paragraph immediately preceding it supplies the needed formal definition: disjoint horizontal bars, one bar per vertex, and adjacency exactly when a vertical segment between the two bars meets at most k bars. The nearby open problems then confirm the intended scope by separating characterization from forbidden-subgraph, regularity, and chromatic-number questions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
